rounds.text: Salona Cotspin Ltd is demonstrating a powerful operational turnaround, highlighted by a staggering 206% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] and a 146% year-on-year net profit surge [E65], which has propelled TTM operating margins up to 6% [E30]. This earnings explosion is backed by pristine cash generation, evidenced by an extraordinary cash conversion ratio of 39.50x and massive operating and free cash flows of ₹79 Cr and ₹69 Cr respectively as of March 2026 [E34, E35, E36]. Fundamental efficiency is rapidly improving as debtor days shortened from 62.0 to 48.8 days and working capital requirements compressed from 16.3 to 10.3 days [E57, E58], while dedicated insiders signal strong internal confidence by expanding promoter shareholding to 68.42% [E40]. Technical momentum fully supports this fundamental acceleration, with the share price positioned comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages in a classic bullish configuration [E47], proving that the market is beginning to notice an enterprise firing on all cylinders. conceded: [E37] and [E42].

Salona Cotspin Ltd carries severe structural and valuation risks that are entirely disconnected from its fundamental earning power. The business is heavily leveraged with a debt-to-equity ratio of 3.15x as of September 2026, driven by borrowings surging to Rs 277 Cr [E37, E38]. This towering debt load is compounded by explicit warnings regarding a low interest coverage ratio and potential capitalization of interest costs [E59, E61]. Furthermore, profitability metrics are deeply anaemic: return on equity sits at a miserable 1.4%, and median ROE over the last year is just 1% [E13, E29]. Long-term profit growth also tells a dismal story, with compounded profit growth over 5 years contracting by -28% and over 3 years plunging by -59% [E19, E20]. Valuation disconnect is glaring, as a discounted cash flow analysis puts intrinsic value at Rs 84 per share against a market price of Rs 263, leaving a staggering negative margin of safety of -211.4% [E42, E43]. Conceded: the company achieved a strong 10-year and 5-year compounded sales growth of 19% and 21% respectively [E14, E15].

Conceded: debt to equity is 3.15x and borrowings reached Rs 277 Cr [E37, E38], alongside warnings of low interest coverage and potential interest capitalization [E59, E61]. However, the bear's focus on weak recent ROE and negative multi-year profit growth ignores the massive operational inflection currently underway, highlighted by a staggering 206% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a net profit surge of 146% year-over-year [E21, E65]. Conceded: DCF places intrinsic value at Rs 84 against the market price of Rs 263 [E42, E43], but static valuation models miss the strong positive momentum in efficiency where debtor days have improved from 62.0 to 48.8 days and working capital requirements reduced to 10.3 days [E57, E58]. Furthermore, profits are fully backed by cash with an exceptional cash conversion of 39.50x, delivering Rs 79 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 69 Cr in free cash flow [E34, E35, E36]. Finally, promoters are backing this turnaround with skin in the game, increasing their holding to 68.42% [E40], while technical structure confirms the stock is trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth is 206% and year-over-year net profit surged 146% [E21, E65], accompanied by rising promoter holdings at 68.42% [E40] and a positive technical alignment above the 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E47]. However, this explosive recent profit metric contrasts sharply with multi-year contractions of -28% over 5 years and -59% over 3 years [E19, E20], indicating the TTM print is a cyclical bounce from a depressed base rather than a durable trend. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 79 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 69 Cr with a 39.50x conversion [E34, E35, E36], alongside working capital and debtor day improvements [E57, E58]. Yet these cash flows are overshadowed by heavy leverage where debt-to-equity sits at 3.15x with borrowings escalating to Rs 277 Cr [E37, E38], explicitly exacerbated by a low interest coverage ratio and potential interest capitalization [E59, E61]. Furthermore, leaning on operational momentum to dismiss valuation is untenable when the reverse DCF requires an ongoing 15.6% earnings growth rate [E44] and the foundational DCF pegs intrinsic value at a severe deficit of Rs 84 per share, resulting in a -211.4% margin of safety [E42, E43].
